source.title: When Do Extended Physics-Informed Neural Networks (XPINNs) Improve Generalization?
source.authors: Zheyuan Hu; Ameya Dilip Jagtap; G. Karniadakis; Kenji Kawaguchi

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some flattened tables and internal result inconsistencies make several model-to-value assignments unclear.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares PINNs and domain-decomposed XPINNs on PDE generalization in a setting outside the listed claim versions and reports experimental outcomes.
record.gate_note: The study compares PINN and XPINN test errors and measures trained-network norm products and theoretical bounds. These results concern PDE solving and domain decomposition; none measures the specific behaviors or systems named in V1–V8. Cited findings from other work were not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests domain decomposition in physics-informed PDE solvers, not any of V1–V8. Its norm-based bounds do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, and using Adam does not constitute an optimizer comparison. A new application of generalization alone does not qualify as T3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly captures the authors' central conclusion: domain decomposition trades simpler subdomain targets against fewer training samples per subnet, so its generalization benefit depends on which factor dominates. The conclusion section's specific examples are internally inconsistent with Section 5; use the experimental sections for task-specific outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares PINN with XPINN domain decomposition for PDE solving; it does not use the original methods underlying the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: PDE task and domain partition; interface and boundary loss weights; the text reports changes in outcomes across these choices.

fits_no_version.finding: PINN and XPINN have similar KdV errors; PINN has lower heat and Poisson errors. Table 3 favors XPINN for advection, although its Results prose swaps the numerical assignments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain decomposition in physics-informed PDE solvers can improve, approximately preserve, or worsen held-out solution error depending on the PDE and training configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: For Euler density, Table 6 reports PINN error 3.4604e-2, XPINN-AM error 1.048e-2, and XPINN-TB error 3.5722e-2; the authors describe AM as better and TB as worse than PINN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The choice of domain partition changes XPINN generalization on the same PDE.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding derivative-interface regularization reduces Poisson error from 4.022e-1 to 1.387e-1; increasing boundary weight further reduces it to 1.108e-1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interface regularization and boundary-loss weighting can improve XPINN solution accuracy without matching the tested PINN baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors compare posterior bounds and trained weight-matrix norms with PDE solution errors, reporting consistent relative orderings across the tested configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Norm-based bounds can indicate relative PINN–XPINN solution accuracy in these PDE experiments.

record.problems: The study uses five fixed random seeds per model, but reports no formal significance tests. Table 3's prose has an apparent contradiction between the stated relative L2 errors and which method performs better. Several table layouts are flattened, and the Euler results do not clearly assign an aggregate XPINN-AM test error.
record.rows_left_out: The study reports separate subnetwork norm complexities and theoretical bounds in Tables 1–6, but these do not directly measure held-out error and the flattened layouts do not reliably support assignments for each subnetwork. They are not included as rows. Additional error-component visualizations and per-subdomain discussion appear in Figures 3, 5, 7, 9, and 11 without separately recoverable numerical results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Matched adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, excessive dropout, and augmentation interactions.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and rankings against norm or margin measures.
Removing examples selected by label memorization versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures address a different claim; this does not mean their PDE errors are unreadable. The study cites an original source associated with V7 but does not test sharpness. No listed version warrants a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

rows.subject: PINN

rows.note: The text explicitly assigns this PINN value; its comparison does not map to a listed version.
rows.check: The reported error is correct, but this PINN–XPINN comparison measures none of V1–V8.

rows.operation_detail: Trained on the KdV PDE task for 5000 epochs using Adam; no regularization.
rows.note: The Results text explicitly reports the XPINN value and says PINN is slightly better.
rows.check: The reported error is correct, but domain decomposition is outside V1–V8.

rows.operation_detail: Trained on the heat equation for 20000 epochs using LBFGS; no regularization.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the advection equation for 5000 epochs using Adam; no regularization.
rows.baseline: XPINN relative L2 error: 1.617e-1±3.582e-2 (as described in Results prose)
rows.note: The prose assigns 2.052e-1 to PINN and 1.617e-1 to XPINN, but says XPINN performs better despite its larger error. The flattened table also leaves assignments uncertain.
rows.check: The value 2.052e-1±1.001e-1 agrees with Table 3's PINN row, not the Results prose as claimed. The prose assigns PINN 1.617e-1 and XPINN 2.052e-1 while claiming XPINN is better. Retain the table-based values and identify the conflicting prose.

rows.subject: XPINN-LMR
rows.size_stated: Three sub-networks; layer and width not stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the advection equation for 5000 epochs; no regularization.
rows.baseline: PINN relative L2 error: 2.052e-1±1.001e-1 (as described in Results prose)
rows.note: The prose reports the XPINN value but contains an apparent direction/value contradiction; the table layout is flattened.
rows.check: The aggregate XPINN value 1.617e-1±3.582e-2 follows Table 3's grouped subnetwork rows, not the prose assignment. Its baseline 2.052e-1 follows the PINN table row. Section 5.3.1 says training procedures are matched, supporting six layers, width 20, tanh, and Adam at 1e-3 for the subnets.

rows.note: The Results text assigns these values and states PINN outperforms XPINN3, XPINN2, and XPINN1.
rows.check: The reported error is correct, but the comparison is outside V1–V8.

rows.operation_detail: Trained on the Poisson equation for 20000 epochs using LBFGS; no regularization.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: 5 hidden layers with 20 neurons in each layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the compressible Euler equations; the optimizer and epoch count are not stated.
rows.baseline: XPINN-AM relative L2 error: not stated
rows.note: Table 6 reports the PINN metric; the prose does not provide an aggregate XPINN-AM error value.
rows.check: The PINN value is correct. Table 6 groups XPINN-A and XPINN-M with aggregate error 1.048e-2±5.3793e-3, supplying the missing baseline. Section 5.5.2 also specifies learning rate 8e-4.

rows.subject: XPINN-AM
rows.size_stated: Five hidden layers with 20 neurons in each layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the compressible Euler equations; the optimizer and epoch count are not stated.
rows.note: The text says XPINN-AM generalizes better than PINN, but Table 6's flattened layout does not support assigning the reported values to an aggregate XPINN-AM error.
rows.check: Table 6's grouped XPINN-A/XPINN-M entries report aggregate density error 1.048e-2±5.3793e-3 and bound 81.09%; the Results prose confirms XPINN-AM improves over PINN. Replace 'not stated' with this error and record learning rate 8e-4. The result still measures no listed version.
